original: Cancer treatment is planned according to the type, stage and biological features of the disease and your personal situation. Through our partner hospital, your case is assessed by a multidisciplinary team in which medical oncologists work closely with surgeons, radiation oncologists and other specialists.
A treatment plan tailored to the type and stage of the disease, agreed in cooperation with surgery, radiation oncology and other departments.
Drug treatments that stop the growth of cancer cells or destroy them, planned individually.
Medicines that act on specific features of cancer cells, used where the tumour biology makes them suitable.
Treatments that help the immune system to recognise and fight cancer cells.
Used for hormone-sensitive cancers, such as some breast and prostate cancers.
Regular follow-up, management of side effects, preserving quality of life and psychosocial support during treatment.
Our partner oncology team treats the following cancers, as well as many other cancer types:
Pathology report and, if available, tissue blocks or slides
Plan your oncology consultation with confidence

Cardiology covers the evaluation, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of heart conditions. Our partner hospital’s cardiology department includes a cardiology outpatient clinic, a coronary intensive care unit, cardiac catheterisation and angiography laboratories, an electrophysiology unit and cardiology laboratories, and works closely with cardiovascular surgery.
Transthoracic and transoesophageal echocardiography to assess the structure and function of the heart.
Treadmill stress test, rhythm Holter, event recorder and tilt-table test.
Coronary angiography, haemodynamic studies and right and left heart catheterisation.
Percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA) and intracoronary stent placement.
Implantation of permanent pacemakers and implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICD).
Electrophysiological studies and radiofrequency ablation to treat heart rhythm disorders.
Mitral and pulmonary balloon valvuloplasty to widen narrowed heart valves.
Percutaneous closure of atrial septal defects (ASD) and patent ductus arteriosus (PDA).
Septal ablation, pericardiocentesis and endomyocardial biopsy.
Previous ECGs, echocardiography or angiography reports
Plan your cardiology consultation with confidence

Orthopaedics and traumatology deal with the diagnosis, treatment and rehabilitation of problems of the bones, joints, muscles and spine in adults and children, including injuries from daily life and sport. Our partner hospital combines experienced orthopaedic surgeons with robotic and navigation technology and works with physical therapy and rehabilitation for a quick return to daily life.
Closed (keyhole) surgery of the knee, shoulder, hip, ankle, elbow and wrist. Recovery is quick and in many cases no hospital stay is needed.
Joint replacement for arthritis performed with robotic technology, special navigation systems and computer assistance.
Joint prostheses for advanced joint wear, for pain-free movement.
Treatment of ligament, meniscus, tendon and cartilage injuries from sport.
Treatment of foot and ankle injuries and conditions.
Surgical treatment of shoulder injuries, instability and wear.
For extensive cartilage damage where other treatments have failed, to preserve the joint and prevent or delay the need for a prosthesis.
Treatment of spinal fractures, infections, tumours and congenital or acquired curvatures.
Treatment of fractures and injuries and their consequences.
Diagnosis and treatment of orthopaedic problems in children.
Diagnosis and treatment of bone and soft tissue tumours.
Plan your orthopaedic consultation with confidence

The wish to have a child is very personal. Our partner IVF centre plans every treatment individually, based on current scientific evidence, and its experienced team of physicians and embryologists decides together on each case. The causes of infertility are investigated carefully first, so that you are spared unnecessary treatment.
Medical history, ultrasound, hormone tests, semen analysis and, if needed, hysteroscopy for both partners.
Ovarian stimulation over about 8 to 14 days, egg collection under anaesthesia, fertilisation in the laboratory and a painless embryo transfer.
IVF in your natural cycle without stimulating medication, for example for women who respond poorly to medication or prefer not to use hormones.
Prepared sperm are placed directly into the uterus around ovulation.
A single sperm is injected into each egg; used for male-factor infertility, including cases with no sperm in the semen (azoospermia).
Sperm with better motility and quality are selected using a microfluidic chip before fertilisation.
Eggs or embryos are frozen for later use, for example before chemotherapy or radiotherapy or to postpone pregnancy.
Embryos are cultured together with supporting cells to support their development in the laboratory.
The outer shell of the embryo is gently thinned or opened to help implantation, for example after repeated unsuccessful transfers.
Embryos can be tested when a parent carries a hereditary disease, so that healthy embryos are selected.
A treatment option that may be considered for selected women with low ovarian reserve.
Special protocols for advanced age, low ovarian reserve, PCOS, endometriosis and repeated IVF failure.
Previous fertility treatments and their results
Hormone and semen analysis results, if available
Plan your fertility consultation with confidence

Neurosurgery covers the surgical diagnosis and treatment of diseases of the brain, spine, spinal cord and nerves. At our partner hospital’s neurological sciences centre, neurosurgeons work in a multidisciplinary team with neurologists, anaesthesiologists, intensive care specialists, radiologists, psychiatrists, psychologists and rehabilitation specialists, in specialised wards and intensive care units.
Microsurgical treatment of tumours of the brain, spinal cord and nerve sheaths, pituitary tumours and skull base tumours.
Treatment of aneurysms, subarachnoid haemorrhage, arteriovenous malformations of the brain and spinal cord and selected strokes, including bypass surgery for blocked brain vessels.
Surgical treatment of epilepsy by a specialised neurology and neurosurgery team, including epilepsy monitoring.
Surgery for lumbar and cervical disc herniation, age-related spinal stenosis and wear, spinal and spinal cord tumours and congenital disorders.
Spine-strengthening procedures for fractures caused by osteoporosis or tumour metastases.
Intrathecal drug pumps for spasticity and pain, and injection treatments for spine-related pain that does not need surgery.
Microsurgical treatment of carpal tunnel syndrome, ulnar and peroneal nerve compression, meralgia paraesthetica and nerve or plexus injuries.
Precise, image-guided procedures on the brain.
Treatment of injuries of the brain, spine and spinal cord.
Surgical treatment of brain and spine conditions in children.
Plan your neurosurgery consultation with confidence

Ophthalmology covers the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of diseases of the eye and its surrounding structures. Our partner hospital’s eye department offers a wide range of specialised units, combining modern technology with experienced specialists.
Treatment of refractive errors with PRK, LASIK, LASEK, Epi-LASIK and IntraLase (femtosecond) LASIK, as well as contact lenses.
Sutureless phacoemulsification under eye-drop anaesthesia with implantation of an intraocular lens.
Diagnosis and treatment of glaucoma to protect the optic nerve.
Diagnosis and treatment of diseases of the retina.
Diagnosis, treatment and surgery of macular diseases.
Diagnosis and treatment of eye damage caused by diabetes.
Diagnosis and treatment of diseases of the cornea.
Specialised care for keratoconus and fitting of special contact lenses.
Treatment of squint and eye problems in children.
Surgery of the eyelids, tear ducts and eye socket, aesthetic surgery around the eyes, and Botox for squint, eyelid spasms or aesthetic purposes.
Conditions affecting both the eye and the nervous system.
Follow-up and treatment of tumours of the eye and its surrounding structures.
Diagnosis and treatment of inflammatory eye diseases, including Behçet’s disease.
Treatment of functional and cosmetic damage after injuries to the eye and its surroundings.
Diagnosis and treatment of eye infections.
Optics, refraction and rehabilitation for patients whose vision cannot be improved further.
Your current glasses or contact lens prescription
Plan your eye consultation with confidence

Organ transplantation can offer a new perspective to patients with end-stage organ failure. Our partner transplant centre works with a multidisciplinary team of transplant surgeons, nephrologists, infectious disease specialists and other physicians, and plans every step from pre-transplant evaluation to long-term follow-up.
For patients with end-stage kidney disease. A two-stage evaluation checks suitability for transplantation and treats any accompanying problems first.
For acute liver failure, end-stage liver disease (cirrhosis) and some liver cancers.
The centre has also performed pancreas and heart transplants; suitability is assessed individually.
For international patients, transplantation is generally performed from a living donor, within the legal requirements, including proof of the relationship between donor and recipient.
Comprehensive medical assessment of recipient and donor, with decisions taken by a multidisciplinary council.
Laparoscopic and minimally invasive transplant techniques, supported by advanced imaging such as multislice CT, 3 Tesla MRI, PET-CT, gamma camera and biplane angiography.
Monitoring, immunosuppressive treatment and long-term follow-up after the transplant.
A strong focus on hygiene and infection prevention, which is particularly important for transplant patients.
Documents for both recipient and potential donor
Blood group and tissue typing results, if available
Plan your transplant consultation with confidence

Gynaecological oncology focuses on cancers and pre-cancerous conditions of the female reproductive organs, from screening and early detection through staging, treatment and long-term follow-up. Care is organised by a multidisciplinary team so that each plan reflects the individual patient. MedLuxLife coordinates your consultation at our partner hospital, arranges translation of your records and stays by your side from first contact to aftercare.
Clear, unhurried discussion of findings, options and next steps with a specialist in gynaecological cancers.
Screening programmes designed to detect changes in the reproductive organs at an early stage.
Assessment of suspicious gynaecological findings, including cases referred from other specialties, to clarify the diagnosis.
Treatment options for gynaecological cancers can include medical therapies and surgery, planned around the stage and type of disease.
Tailored management across the full spectrum of reproductive system tumours, from early lesions to invasive disease.
Diagnostic and treatment procedures for early cell changes of the cervix.
HPV vaccination and other preventive vaccines as part of a prevention-focused approach.
Evaluation and risk management for families with hereditary cancer syndromes affecting the reproductive organs.
A structured follow-up plan after treatment, which MedLuxLife can help you continue at home.
Differential diagnosis of benign gynaecological masses
Recent smear (Pap) test, HPV and biopsy reports
Previous pelvic ultrasound, CT or MRI images and reports
Plan your Gynaecological Oncology consultation with confidence

Haematology covers the diagnosis and treatment of blood disorders, both malignant and non-malignant. At our partner hospital, haematologists work closely with immunology, genetics, haematopathology, infectious diseases, biochemistry and radiology, supported by a strong laboratory. MedLuxLife organises your appointments, prepares your medical files in advance and supports you and your family throughout treatment abroad.
Clinical experience combined with modern laboratory methods helps to reach a reliable diagnosis without unnecessary delay.
Cases are discussed with immunology, genetics, haematopathology, infectious diseases, biochemistry and radiology specialists.
Treatment planning for leukaemias, lymphomas, plasma cell disorders and related conditions.
Assessment and management of anaemias, haemoglobinopathies and other benign blood conditions.
Chemotherapy is given by experienced nurses who are attentive to the physical and emotional needs of patients with blood cancers.
Transplantation using the patient’s own stem cells, alongside conventional treatment where appropriate.

Transplantation from a suitable sibling donor. Indications can include acute and chronic leukaemias, lymphomas, multiple myeloma, aplastic anaemia, myelodysplastic syndrome, thalassaemia and sickle cell anaemia.
Recent full blood count and other blood test results
Bone marrow biopsy reports, if available
Plan your Haematology consultation with confidence

Coordinates assessment, decision-making, treatment and follow-up for patients who are being considered for, or are undergoing, a transplant, reviewing previous treatment, imaging, pathology and laboratory findings together.
Collects stem cells from the blood as part of the transplant process.
Processes stem cells and stores them cryogenically in nitrogen tanks, with separate quarantine and main storage, using an automated freezing system.
Analyses blood and marrow cells to support diagnosis, treatment planning and assessment of the response to treatment.
Performs tissue typing used to assess compatibility between patient and donor.
Works alongside a genetic diagnosis centre so that genetic findings can inform diagnosis and treatment decisions.
Treatment takes place in single rooms within a dedicated unit with HEPA air filtration throughout, controlled disinfection on entry and beds that can be converted for emergency care.
Rooms are designed with views and patient comfort in mind to support psychological wellbeing during a long hospital stay.
Patients are monitored closely at every stage, and follow-up continues after discharge with the involvement of social support teams.
Haematology and pathology reports, including bone marrow biopsy results
Details of previous chemotherapy or other treatment received
Plan your Adult Bone Marrow Transplantation consultation with confidence

Bone marrow (stem cell) transplantation is a complex, multi-stage treatment that calls for close teamwork between laboratories, clinical units and nursing staff. The transplant clinic at our partner hospital brings these stages together under one roof, from diagnostic work-up and treatment planning to follow-up after discharge. MedLuxLife helps adult patients and their families arrange the evaluation with the specialists and stay well informed throughout a lengthy treatment journey.

Nuclear medicine uses small amounts of radioactive substances to image and treat disease at a molecular level, giving information about how organs function as well as how they look. The department at our partner hospital works with many specialties, including cardiology, nephrology, orthopaedics, oncology and endocrinology, and has been designed to keep radiation exposure for patients and staff to a minimum. MedLuxLife coordinates referrals, scan appointments and the transfer of results to your treating doctors.
Scans that can support the diagnosis of certain strokes, dementia and hydrocephalus, and help locate the seizure focus before epilepsy surgery.
Imaging to investigate pulmonary embolism and to estimate remaining lung function before lung surgery.
Bone imaging to reveal hidden fractures, bone infection and bone metastases.
Studies to assess coronary artery disease and to evaluate the heart after bypass surgery or stenting.
Imaging to look for urinary tract obstruction, urine reflux towards the kidneys and kidney infection, and to support kidney transplantation.
Scans that help distinguish benign from malignant lesions, stage tumours, guide biopsy sites, detect recurrence, assess response to chemotherapy and plan radiotherapy.
Investigations of goitre, oesophageal, stomach and gallbladder disease, acute intestinal bleeding, hidden infection, lymphatic drainage, tear ducts and salivary gland function.
Spacious rooms, zoned layout according to radiation levels and daylight-style lighting in treatment rooms are intended to support comfort and safety.
Locating the epileptic focus before epilepsy surgery
Assessment of lung reserve before lung surgery
Evaluation after bypass surgery or stent placement
Investigating urine reflux to the kidneys
Previous scan images on CD or via download link, with reports
Recent kidney function and, where relevant, thyroid blood test results
Plan your Nuclear Medicine consultation with confidence

Cardiovascular surgery treats diseases of the heart and major blood vessels, from coronary artery disease and valve problems to congenital heart defects and aortic disease. The department at our partner hospital offers surgery for both adults and children, with dedicated intensive care and a sterile operating environment. MedLuxLife arranges a review of your cardiac tests by the surgical team before travel, so you understand the proposed approach in advance.
Conventional bypass surgery and beating-heart bypass surgery for narrowed coronary arteries.
Repair or prosthetic replacement of the aortic, mitral and tricuspid valves.
Surgical repair in children and adults, including ASD, VSD, PDA, aortic coarctation, Ebstein’s anomaly, tetralogy of Fallot and transposition of the great arteries (TGA).
Surgery for aortic aneurysms of the ascending aorta, arch and descending aorta, including combined procedures, and for acute and chronic aortic dissection.
Surgical treatment of diseases affecting the arteries and veins outside the heart.
Heart transplantation, artificial heart pumps and anti-remodelling surgery for advanced heart failure.
Removal of the pericardium, the sac around the heart, when it restricts heart function.
Surgical removal of tumours of the heart.
Second and third operations for patients who have had previous heart or vascular surgery.
Echocardiography, ECG and coronary angiography reports and images
Operation notes from any previous heart surgery
Plan your Cardiovascular Surgery consultation with confidence

Interventional radiology uses imaging such as ultrasound, CT and angiography to guide minimally invasive diagnostic and therapeutic procedures. Interventional radiologists not only diagnose disease but also take an active part in its treatment, often through a small puncture rather than open surgery. MedLuxLife coordinates your assessment at our partner hospital, including pre-procedure tests, and supports you through recovery and travel home.
Fine-needle aspiration and Tru-cut biopsies guided by ultrasound and/or CT for the neck and thyroid, chest, abdominal organs and bones.
Contrast imaging of arteries, usually via the femoral artery, with high-resolution and 3D imaging to show even small vessel branches.
Imaging of veins to investigate thrombosis, tumour blockages and adrenal tumours, or to assess the saphenous vein before bypass surgery.
Non-vascular interventions such as thoracentesis, abscess drainage and stenting of tracheobronchial narrowing.
Biliary drainage and stenting, nephrostomy, ureteral stenting, cyst and abscess drainage and RF ablation.
Balloon and stent treatment of narrowed or blocked arteries throughout the body, from the carotid and brain vessels to the legs.
Coil embolisation of brain aneurysms, embolisation of AVMs and fistulas, and intra-arterial thrombolysis in acute stroke within a limited time window.
Embolisation for nosebleeds, coughing up blood and acute gastrointestinal bleeding, and for head and neck tumours.
Covered stents for aneurysms of the thoracic and abdominal aorta and for pseudoaneurysms in peripheral arteries.
Transarterial chemoembolisation and RF ablation for liver tumours, portal vein interventions and venous port placement.
Venous angioplasty and stenting, dialysis catheters, fistula angioplasty, vena cava filters, TIPS and venous catheters.
Uterine fibroid embolisation and diabetic foot
Fibroid embolisation as an alternative to surgery, and balloon and laser angioplasty for narrowed foot vessels in diabetes.
Fine-needle aspiration and Tru-cut biopsy of neck masses and thyroid nodules
Renal angiography (including before and after kidney transplantation)
Saphenous vein venography before bypass surgery
Balloon angioplasty and stenting of vascular stenoses
Brachiocephalic and aortoiliac angioplasty and stenting
Iliac, femoral and popliteal artery angioplasty
Embolisation of cerebral aneurysms (direct or balloon-assisted coiling)
Embolisation of cranial and extracranial arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) and fistulas (AVFs)
Embolisation for epistaxis, haemoptysis and acute gastrointestinal bleeding
Endograft treatment of peripheral aneurysms and pseudoaneurysms
Angioplasty and stenting of venous stenoses
Venous catheter placement (permanent tunnelled and temporary)
Balloon and laser angioplasty for diabetic foot
Previous CT, MRI or angiography images and reports
Recent blood clotting and kidney function results
Plan your Interventional Radiology consultation with confidence

Neurology focuses on disorders of the brain, spinal cord, nerves and muscles in both adults and children. Through our partner hospital, MedLuxLife arranges access to specialised neurology units, from stroke and epilepsy care to sleep and balance disorders. We coordinate your appointments, translate your records and stay at your side throughout diagnosis and follow-up.
Assessment and treatment planning for a broad range of nerve, brain and muscle complaints in adults and children.
Rapid evaluation of cerebrovascular events, followed by neurological intensive care, rehabilitation and measures for secondary prevention after a stroke.
Diagnostic work-up may include long-term video-EEG, neuropsychological assessment, MRI, PET-CT and SPECT, as well as pre-surgical evaluation where surgery is considered.
Investigation of recurring or persistent headaches and migraine, with an individual treatment plan.
Neurological care for patients with tumours of the brain and nervous system, in cooperation with other specialties.
Evaluation of memory loss and cognitive decline, supported by the neuropsychology and neurocognitive laboratories.
Diagnosis, treatment planning and long-term follow-up for people living with MS.
Assessment and management of Parkinson’s disease, tremor and other movement disorders.
Investigation of muscle weakness and nerve disorders, including EMG testing.
Evaluation in a dedicated sleep disorders laboratory for sleep-related complaints.
Balance laboratory assessment, including posturography, to help find the cause of dizziness.
Neuropsychological assessment plus EEG, EMG and transcranial magnetic stimulation, a neurocognitive laboratory and intraoperative imaging and monitoring methods.
Previous brain or spine MRI/CT images on CD or via link
Earlier EEG or EMG reports, if available
Plan your Neurology consultation with confidence

Algology, or pain medicine, focuses on identifying the source of chronic pain and building a treatment plan around the individual, including pain whose cause is difficult to pin down. At our partner hospital, a pain specialist examines each patient in detail before recommending options, which may combine medical, interventional and lifestyle measures. MedLuxLife arranges the consultation, shares your records in advance and coordinates any follow-up.
Assessment and personalised management of long-standing pain, with the aim of finding its underlying cause.
Image-guided and needle-based procedures that target the structures thought to be generating pain.
Pain control tailored to people living with cancer, coordinated with their wider treatment.
A needle-based therapy that may be used alongside other approaches to help relieve muscular and chronic pain.
Medical ozone treatment, including autohaemotherapy, offered as part of selected pain treatment plans.
A minimally invasive endoscopic examination of the epidural space that can be used in the assessment and treatment of certain back and leg pain.
Injection of medication into the epidural space, which may help reduce inflammation-related spinal and radiating pain.
Targeted injections that interrupt pain signals along specific nerves or the sympathetic nervous system, which may provide longer-term relief in suitable patients.
Controlled heat delivered by radio waves to selected nerves to reduce the transmission of pain.
Recent spinal or joint imaging (MRI, CT) with reports
A list of pain medication currently taken and previous pain treatments
Plan your Algology (Pain Medicine) consultation with confidence

Psychiatry is concerned with the evaluation, diagnosis and treatment of mental health problems, looking at emotional, cognitive and behavioural symptoms as a whole. The department offers support for difficulties ranging from stress and life challenges to more serious mental health conditions, with treatment plans tailored to each person. MedLuxLife can arrange confidential consultations at our partner hospital, including interpreter support where needed.
A comprehensive assessment that considers medical history, symptoms and living circumstances to understand underlying causes.
Medication may be prescribed where appropriate, with regular follow-up to monitor its effect and safety.
Talking therapies including cognitive behavioural therapy, psychoanalysis, family therapy and group therapy.
Prompt support in psychiatric emergencies such as suicidal thoughts, acute anxiety attacks or psychotic symptoms.
Programmes for people with long-term mental health conditions, focusing on daily living skills, work and social integration.
List of current and previous psychiatric medications
Plan your Psychiatry consultation with confidence

Health includes emotional, cognitive and mental wellbeing as well as physical health. The clinical psychology unit offers psychological assessment and support for children, adolescents and adults, including school-related assessments, structured education programmes and therapy for patients undergoing cancer treatment. MedLuxLife can arrange appointments at our partner hospital and help with language and scheduling.
Help with a wide range of emotional, behavioural and developmental difficulties, using cognitive behavioural therapy and play therapy.
Assessment of attention, learning and reading difficulties, followed by individual training plans based on the results.
Developmental screening tests, intelligence tests, learning difficulty tests and attention tests.
Individual attention-enhancing programmes and reading disorder (dyslexia) programmes for children.
Cognitive behavioural approaches for behaviour problems, family conflict, mood difficulties and exam anxiety.
Cognitive behavioural therapy for depression, anxiety, OCD, panic, trauma, and family, relationship or work-related problems.
Patients treated in the oncology unit are invited to psychotherapy, including cognitive behavioural therapy and meaning-centred therapy for cancer and grief, to help them adapt and cope.
Seminars for parents and children can be organised at the request of schools.
Children: toilet problems (toilet training, stool withholding, soiling)
Children: family difficulties such as divorce or bereavement (post-traumatic stress)
Children: physical complaints such as abdominal pain or nausea
Adults: bereavement, accidents or divorce (post-traumatic stress)
School reports or teacher feedback (for children)
Plan your Psychology consultation with confidence

Physical therapy and rehabilitation aims to restore movement and function, reduce pain and improve mobility after injury, illness or surgery. The department offers assessment, treatment and rehabilitation for a wide range of conditions, from musculoskeletal disorders to neurological diseases, along with several specialised programmes. MedLuxLife can arrange a rehabilitation stay at our partner hospital and coordinate it with your other treatment.
Treatment for arthritis, osteoporosis, inflammatory and soft tissue rheumatic diseases, and neck, back and lower back pain.
Rehabilitation after fractures and dislocations, sports injuries, spinal curvatures, foot problems and orthopaedic surgery such as joint replacement.
Programmes for stroke, brain and spinal cord injury, facial paralysis, nerve injuries, muscle diseases and Parkinson’s disease.
Therapy for children with spasticity, aimed at improving movement and daily function.
Supervised exercise and recovery programmes following heart problems.
A stress incontinence programme for urinary leakage and guided exercise during pregnancy.
Educational programmes teaching posture, movement and exercise to protect the spine and bones.
Group-based therapy and education for people living with fibromyalgia.
Rehabilitation after cosmetic surgery, programmes for dialysis patients, and assessment and planning after obesity surgery.
Therapy options for excessive sweating in specific areas of the body.
Inflammatory joint diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis
Soft tissue rheumatic diseases such as fibromyalgia and myofascial pain syndrome
Neck, back and lower back pain
Joint stiffness and circulatory problems after fractures or dislocations
Meniscus and ligament injuries and other sports injuries
Flat feet and other foot problems
Rehabilitation before and after orthopaedic surgery, including joint replacement
Assessment and planning after obesity surgery
Surgical or discharge reports from recent operations
Plan your Physical Therapy and Rehabilitation consultation with confidence

Rheumatology is a subspecialty dedicated to the diagnosis and treatment of rheumatic diseases, which are common, often long-lasting and can lead to pain, loss of function and reduced quality of life if not managed appropriately. Because these conditions can affect many organs, care is coordinated with several other specialties. MedLuxLife arranges consultations and follow-up at our partner hospital and keeps your records organised between visits.
Specialist evaluation of joint pain, stiffness, inflammation and related symptoms to establish an accurate diagnosis.
Individual treatment plans aimed at controlling symptoms, preserving function and supporting quality of life.
Joint care with dermatology, neurology, orthopaedics and traumatology, physical therapy and rehabilitation, and ophthalmology when several organs are involved.
Treatment for widespread pain and fatigue planned jointly by rheumatologists, physical therapy and rehabilitation specialists, psychiatrists and neurologists.
Previous blood tests, including inflammatory markers and antibody results
List of current medications, including biologic therapies
Plan your Rheumatology consultation with confidence
Nephrologists evaluate, treat and follow patients with declining kidney function, aiming to slow damage and, where possible, reverse it.
Examination, tests, imaging and medical history are reviewed carefully to establish whether kidney damage is irreversible.
A systematic review of all organ systems, with particular attention to heart and blood vessel health, to identify any reasons a transplant may not be advisable.
Coexisting conditions found during the assessment are treated before transplantation is planned.
For suitable patients, a kidney may be transplanted from a living donor following assessment.
Transplantation from a deceased donor is the alternative option for suitable patients.
Recent kidney function tests and dialysis records
Blood group and any previous tissue typing results
Plan your Kidney Transplant Clinic consultation with confidence

Learning that kidney damage is permanent can be a difficult moment, and careful confirmation of the diagnosis comes first. The kidney transplant team at our partner hospital aims to protect kidney function for as long as possible and, where kidney failure reaches its final stage, assesses whether a transplant is a suitable option. MedLuxLife coordinates the evaluation for both recipient and donor, organises appointments and travel, and supports you through follow-up.

Liver transplantation is a treatment option for acute liver failure, end-stage liver disease (cirrhosis) with permanent damage, and certain liver cancers. For many patients it can offer the possibility of returning to a more active life. MedLuxLife arranges the assessment at our partner hospital, coordinates the paperwork and travel for patient and family, and stays in contact throughout recovery.
Assessment of whether transplantation is appropriate when the liver stops working suddenly.
Evaluation of patients with advanced, irreversible liver damage.
Transplantation may be considered for selected cancers of the liver.
A multidisciplinary team reviews each case to decide whether transplantation is suitable and to plan the next steps.
Guidance on the hospital stay and recovery after transplantation, with follow-up that MedLuxLife helps you continue at home.
Recent liver function tests and imaging reports
Previous liver biopsy or endoscopy reports, if available
Plan your Liver Transplant Clinic consultation with confidence

pages: Thyroid and Parathyroid Diseases and Surgery Clinic
Thyroid and Parathyroid Diseases and Surgery Clinic

original: This clinic focuses on parathyroid transplantation, a treatment option for patients with permanent hypoparathyroidism, and on the diagnosis and treatment of parathyroid gland diseases more broadly. Endocrine surgeons work alongside endocrinology, immunology and bioengineering specialists. MedLuxLife can arrange an initial evaluation of your case at our partner hospital and coordinate every step if transplantation is considered suitable.
A licensed transplant procedure, classed as an organ transplant, that may be considered for patients with permanent hypoparathyroidism.
An endocrine surgeon specialised in parathyroid transplantation reviews your history and explains whether the procedure is an option for you.
Diagnosis and treatment of a range of parathyroid disorders beyond transplantation.
Endocrine surgery, endocrinology, immunology and transplantation, and genetic bioengineering specialists work together on each case.
A dedicated transplant coordinator supports the process, alongside MedLuxLife’s own case management.
Recent calcium, PTH and vitamin D blood results
Previous thyroid or parathyroid surgery reports
Plan your Parathyroid Transplant Clinic consultation with confidence

Obstetrics and gynaecology covers women’s health at every stage of life, from fertility and pregnancy to menopause and gynaecological oncology. MedLuxLife arranges consultations, diagnostics and treatment with specialists at our partner hospital, who work together with radiology, psychiatry and other departments when needed. We take care of scheduling, translation and travel so you can concentrate on your health.
Evaluation of couples who have difficulty conceiving, with treatment planned at the appropriate time.
Standard IVF plus microinjection, TESA, TESE, co-culture, in vitro maturation, assisted hatching and preimplantation genetic diagnosis, with research activities including stem cell research.
Investigation of recurrent pregnancy loss and repeated unsuccessful IVF attempts.
Support during menopause, including mammography, bone density measurement and psychological counselling in cooperation with radiology and psychiatry.
Care for pregnancy from preconception through birth and the postpartum period, including higher-risk pregnancies.
Screening for chromosomal and structural anomalies, 3D ultrasound and invasive perinatal procedures where indicated.
Counselling, screening, differential diagnosis and medical and surgical treatment of gynaecological tumours.
Diagnosis of hereditary cancer risk with preventive and therapeutic approaches, including protective and therapeutic vaccination.
Genetic counselling for families with a history of hereditary disease
Counselling after a difficult obstetric history
Consultation and differential diagnosis of suspected gynaecological cases
Medical and surgical treatment of gynaecological cancers
Treatment of pre-invasive, borderline and invasive tumours of the reproductive system
Protective and therapeutic vaccinations in gynaecological oncology
Diagnosis of familial cancers with preventive and therapeutic approaches
Diagnosis and treatment of pre-invasive lesions of the cervix
Previous ultrasound, smear or hormone test results
Pregnancy records or earlier IVF treatment summaries, if applicable
Plan your Obstetrics and Gynaecology consultation with confidence

Perinatology, a division of obstetrics and gynaecology, focuses on the health of mother and baby during pregnancy. Alongside routine pregnancy care and delivery, it provides follow-up and management of high-risk pregnancies and the diagnosis and management of maternal and fetal conditions using specialised scans, tests and procedures. MedLuxLife helps expectant parents arrange screening, specialist scans and consultations at our partner hospital and coordinates every step of the visit.
Pregnancy follow-up and delivery, with closer monitoring and management for high-risk pregnancies.

An ultrasound nuchal translucency measurement, which can be combined with blood tests and further markers such as the fetal nasal bone, blood flow in the fetal heart and the facial angle, to assess the risk of Down syndrome and other conditions.
A triple or quadruple blood test that estimates risk; a raised result indicates that diagnostic testing may be advisable, not that the baby is affected.
A detailed transvaginal ultrasound examination of fetal development early in pregnancy.
A high-resolution second-level ultrasound examining fetal organs and growth, which can include uterine artery Doppler and cervical length assessment in at-risk pregnancies.

A detailed examination of the baby’s heart structure and function, recommended when there is an increased risk of congenital heart disease or a suspected abnormality; ideally performed around 18-21 weeks.
Maternal and fetal Doppler examinations to assess blood flow to the placenta and within the baby’s circulation.
A placental tissue sample, usually taken at 11-14 weeks under ultrasound guidance, to examine chromosome number and structure.
A small sample of amniotic fluid, usually taken at 16-22 weeks, for chromosomal analysis; rapid FISH testing for selected chromosomes may give preliminary results sooner.
A small blood sample from the umbilical cord vein, usually after the 19th week, for diagnostic testing.
Results are discussed with parents, and findings such as a heart abnormality help plan where and how the birth should take place.
15-21 week screening tests (triple or quadruple test)
11-14 week transvaginal detailed fetal anomaly screening
Maternity record (e.g. Mutterpass) and previous pregnancy scan reports
Previous screening or genetic test results
Plan your Perinatology consultation with confidence

Chronic pelvic pain can affect every part of daily life, and finding its cause often requires more than one specialist. This multidisciplinary clinic investigates the nature and origin of pelvic pain, including endometriosis, using diagnostic methods chosen according to each patient’s symptoms, and then plans treatment based on current medical evidence. MedLuxLife arranges your evaluation at our partner hospital and supports you with preparation, records and travel.
A structured consultation explores when, where and how the pain occurs, its intensity and its effect on work and daily life.
Diagnostic methods are selected to match each patient’s symptoms in order to identify the cause of the pain.
Assessment of endometriosis as a possible cause of pelvic pain, followed by individual treatment planning.

The clinic at our partner hospital takes a multidisciplinary approach to identifying the cause and planning suitable treatment. MedLuxLife arranges a discreet, well-prepared visit and coordinates every step of your stay.
A structured evaluation to identify why excess hair growth has developed, as the basis for any treatment plan.
Specialists from related fields work together on diagnosis and treatment planning.
Assessment of associated changes such as hair loss, acne, a deepening voice or increased muscle mass, which may occur alone or together.
Guidance on distinguishing the relative increase in hair growth that can occur normally after menopause from findings that need further investigation.
Treatment is planned according to the cause identified and the patient’s personal situation.
Recognition that untreated hirsutism can affect self-confidence, social life and mood, with care that takes these concerns seriously.

Audiology covers the detailed assessment and rehabilitation of hearing and balance problems in babies, children and adults. The department at our partner hospital offers a broad range of hearing and vestibular tests, including objective tests suitable for infants and for people with dizziness. MedLuxLife helps families schedule tests at suitable times, explains preparation requirements in advance and arranges for results to be shared with your doctors at home.
Screening of babies’ hearing using BERA so that possible hearing loss can be identified early.

An objective electrophysiological test that measures the auditory nerve’s response to sound through electrodes placed on the head, used especially for infants who did not pass screening, babies with risk factors and children with speech delay who cannot complete other tests. It is also known as ABR, BAEP or BAER.
TEOAE/DPOAE and auditory steady-state response testing, which can support and complement BERA findings.
Age-appropriate hearing tests including behavioural observation audiometry, visual reinforcement audiometry and play audiometry, as well as free field testing.
Pure-tone and speech audiometry, plus high-frequency audiometry where indicated.
Middle ear and Eustachian tube tests
Tympanometry and acoustic reflex testing, high-frequency (1000 Hz) tympanometry for babies up to six months, and Eustachian tube function testing.
Records eye movements with video goggles during oculomotor, positional and caloric tests to help determine whether dizziness originates in the inner ear or the brain.
Assesses the vestibulo-ocular reflex of each semicircular canal separately.
Vestibular evoked myogenic potentials, used in the differential diagnosis of conditions such as semicircular canal dehiscence, early Meniere’s disease and otolith organ dysfunction.
Caloric vestibular testing (ENG) and rotational examination to evaluate the function of each balance organ and central compensation.
When benign paroxysmal positional vertigo is identified, corrective manoeuvres such as Epley, Vannucchi, Gufoni and BBQ roll may be performed.

The test is usually done during natural sleep without medication, so babies are brought awake and fasted for feeding and sleep at the clinic; evening appointments, or testing under general anaesthesia with an anaesthetist at the family’s request, may be arranged.
Conditions that tests can help evaluate
Hearing loss in babies, children and adults
Speech and language delay with suspected hearing loss
Balance problems after traumatic brain injury
Previous hearing test results and audiograms
Newborn screening results and birth history for infants

Endocrine surgery treats disorders of the hormone-producing glands, mainly the thyroid, parathyroid and adrenal glands, when too much or too little hormone is produced or when a growth needs removal. These delicate operations require careful technique to protect the voice, calcium balance and surrounding structures. MedLuxLife arranges your consultation with the surgical team at our partner hospital and plans your stay around surgery and recovery; hormone results and scans go directly to the doctors.
